arantella: A lively Italian folk dance, performed here as a fancy-dress entertainment.
macaroons: Small sweet biscuits made from almonds, sugar, and egg white.
tambourine: A small hand drum with metal jingles set in its frame.
skylark: A small brown songbird, used here as a pet name for Nora.
singing-bird: A bird kept in a cage for its song, here a term of affection.
songbird: A bird that sings, here a term of affection for Nora.
squirrel: A small rodent, used here as a playful pet name for Nora.
cloak: A loose outer garment without sleeves, worn over other clothes.
shawl: A large piece of cloth worn over the shoulders for warmth.
fancy-dress: Costume worn to a party, pretending to be a character.
domino: A loose hooded cloak worn at masked balls, also a costume.
shilling: Old British coin worth one-twentieth of a pound.
pounds: Units of British money used here as a sum of cash.
penny: A small old British coin, worth one-twelfth of a shilling.
spendthrift: A person who spends money recklessly and wastefully.
salary: Fixed regular payment a person receives for their work.
clerk: An office worker who keeps records and handles paperwork.
lease: A legal agreement allowing someone to rent a property for a time.
book-keeping: Recording money received and spent in a business's accounts.
subordinate: A person of lower rank who works under someone else.
lucrative: Bringing in a large amount of money; very profitable.
diseased: Affected by illness or disease, unhealthy in body.
wreckage: Broken pieces of a ship or other object after a disaster.
shipwrecked: Having lost a ship at sea through a wreck or disaster.
hoarse: Having a rough, weak voice, as from shouting or strain.
banquet: A formal, elaborate dinner held for many guests.
maiden: An unmarried young woman, often a girl.
bride: A woman on her wedding day or just after marriage.
invisible: Impossible to see, hidden from view.
scientific: Relating to careful study and testing of the natural world.
narrow-minded: Unwilling to consider other people's ideas or opinions.
self-willed: Determined to do things one's own way, ignoring others.
imprudent: Acting without care or thought for the consequences.
tiresome: Annoying and tedious, causing weariness or irritation.
disagreeable: Unpleasant, rude, or difficult to get along with.
expedient: Convenient and useful for a purpose, though not necessarily right.
obstinate: Stubbornly refusing to change one's mind or give way.
hypocrite: A person who pretends to hold virtues they do not really have.
heartless: Cruel and without pity or feeling for others.
tactless: Careless in speech, likely to upset or offend people.
dismissal: Being sent away from a job or position by an employer.
forged: Copied or faked dishonestly, especially a signature or document.
pretence: A false appearance or behaviour meant to deceive others.
procured: Obtained or acquired something, often with some effort.
presume: To suppose or assume something is true without proof.
daresay: I suppose or expect; probably, in an informal way.
smothered: Suppressed or held back, not allowed to be expressed.
stifled: Suppressed or held back, kept from being seen or heard.
court: To try to win someone's love or favour, as a suitor.
sacred: Deeply respected and treated as holy or very important.
conscience: An inner sense of right and wrong guiding one's actions.
doll-child: A child treated like a doll; Nora's name for herself.
spite: In spite of: despite, without being stopped by something.
wretched: Very unhappy, miserable, or in a sad state.
chirp: A short, high sound made by small birds.
